page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Page number "(44)" at the head. Heading "SECT. III." with subtitle "De Vocalibus & Dipthongis." Below them, opening paragraph with drop capital V. Then a table of five rows (Nomen, Figura, Potestas), with Hebrew glyphs left of the Latin names and Hebrew vowel figures in the middle column. Below the table, two paragraphs. Catchword "non" at the lower right.

main_text.head: SECT. III.
De Vocalibus & Dipthongis.
main_text.p: Vocales sunt quinque, quas exprimunt tum per figuras tum per puncta.
main_text.l: [illegible, ~3 letters] Pethoco. | a | [illegible, ~2 letters] | Pathac Hebr.
[illegible, ~3 letters] Revotfo. | e | [illegible, ~3 letters] | Tfere & fegol.
[illegible, ~3 letters] Zequafo. | o | [illegible, ~2 letters] | ] vel Cametz Chatuph
[illegible, ~3 letters] Otfotfo. | u | [illegible, ~3 letters] vel [illegible, ~2 letters] | ] vel Kibbuts.
main_text.p: Olim punctum unicum omnes vocales repræ-sentabat, quod supra literam significabat a, o, vel u; sub litera, e vel i: at postea vocales à Græ-cis mutuatæ.
Figuræ vocalium pro libitu nunc infra, nunc supra literam collocantur: Puncta vero situm.

page.notes: The Hebrew names and vowel figures in the Nomen and Figura columns are printed Hebrew and could not be read letter by letter, so each is marked illegible. The Latin names (Pethoco, Revotfo, Chevotfo, Zequafo, Otfotfo) and the vowel letters a, e, i, o, u are copied as printed. The table's Potestas cell for the first row wraps to "Hebr."; the "1" before "vel" in the last two rows is a printed Hebrew sign that is uncertain. The final word of the last line reads "situm" with a long s; the page's lower right shows the catchword "non". The top right of the scan has a small mark that is not text.
